verdict.rationale: Maritime publishes dedicated first-party framework pages for both Claude Code and Codex. They describe running each in its own cloud micro-VM with persistent storage, and say Codex works with no key using Maritime's metered LLM access. Together with the ready-made framework templates, this is a vendor-supplied recipe for running these coding agents inside its sandbox. Missing for 10: detailed step-by-step recipe content in the evidence (setup commands, auth flow for Claude Code), and any independent or hands-on corroboration that the recipes work as described.

support.subject: As an ai-native user, I can run coding agents like Claude Code or Codex inside the sandbox following the vendor's own recipe

citations.quote: Maritime gives it what a laptop session can't: its own always-on micro-VM in the cloud, persistent storage, sleep/wake economics, and every chat channel Maritime supports.
No key is required: the agent uses Maritime's metered LLM access by default.
Every ready-made template is a real agent framework, pre-configured and one image pull from live. Pick one, name it, deploy.
